01 / CASE STUDIES

Athletic retail, regional media, and municipal community programs. Each structured as an exclusive category agreement, and each built to renew.

SWIPE TO EXPLORE
CASE 01 / ATHLETIC RETAIL
Track Shack
Running & walking events, Orlando FL
4→10
EVENTS, YEAR ONE TO YEAR TWO
OBJECTIVE

Own the internet category across Track Shack's event calendar and reach a health and fitness focused audience in a priority market.

STRUCTURE

Exclusive provider status secured mile marker branding, barricade signage, start and finish line placement, plus live event announcements. Running shoe gift card giveaways drove lead capture and attendee demographic data.

EXECUTION

Launched with four events. Turnout and demographic fit built the internal case to scale, and the program expanded to ten events the following year.

More than doubled event footprint in one cycle, driven by results rather than relationship alone.
CASE 02 / MEDIA & PUBLISHING
Orlando Weekly
Regional media event series, Orlando FL
6×
EVENTS PER YEAR, RECURRING
OBJECTIVE

Extend reach past the event footprint by partnering with a media outlet that brought its own owned audience to the table.

STRUCTURE

Exclusive internet provider status included event signage, logo placement on digital flyers, website presence, and inclusion in email blasts, pairing on-site activation with a publisher's distribution.

EXECUTION

Ran lead capture, audience data collection, and promotional giveaways at a recurring bi-monthly to quarterly cadence.

Turned a sponsorship into a media channel: event-day presence plus a publisher's digital reach.

03 / APPROACH

How I think
about partnerships

Four things I have learned running sponsorships that had to justify their own renewal.

01

Exclusivity is worth more than volume

Owning a category outright at ten events beats sharing it at fifty. Exclusive status is what turns a logo into a position, and it is the first thing I structure for.

02

The renewal is built in year one

Partners re-sign for programs that produced. Every activation I run is instrumented from day one with lead capture, demographic data, and cost per lead, so the expansion conversation is a numbers conversation rather than a favor.

03

A partner's channels are part of the deal

On-site presence reaches the people who showed up. Email lists, digital flyers, website placement, and social reach everyone who did not. The partnerships that outperform are the ones where I negotiated for both.

04

Fit beats reach

An audience that matches the market is worth more than a bigger one that does not. I validate demographic alignment before scaling spend, which is how a four-event pilot becomes a ten-event program instead of an expensive lesson.
